signature.name: Zocalo
signature.detail: The vast main square is the heart of Mexico City and the natural starting point for any first visit, ringed by the National Palace and the cathedral. Come early in the morning for cooler air and fewer crowds, and note that the flag ceremony happens here daily.

signature.name: Metropolitan Cathedral of Mexico City
signature.detail: This enormous colonial cathedral anchors the Zocalo and is one of the most important churches in the Americas. It is free to enter but modest dress is expected, and it sits right beside the metro and the square.

signature.name: National Palace
signature.detail: The seat of the federal government faces the Zocalo and is famous for the murals inside. Bring photo ID for entry, check opening hours in advance, and go on a weekday morning to avoid queues.

signature.name: Chapultepec Castle
signature.detail: Perched on the hill in Chapultepec Park, this castle offers city views and grand rooms that make it a top stop. Arrive when it opens to beat the line, and be ready for a steep walk up or a short park train ride.

signature.name: National Museum of Anthropology
signature.detail: One of the world's great museums, with the Aztec Sun Stone and vast halls on Mexico's ancient cultures. Allow at least half a day, and note that it is usually closed on Mondays.

signature.name: Frida Kahlo Museum
signature.detail: The Blue House in Coyoacan draws visitors from around the world to see where Kahlo lived and worked. Book timed tickets online well ahead, as walk-up entry is often sold out.

signature.name: Basilica of Our Lady of Guadalupe
signature.detail: The most visited Catholic shrine in the Americas, home to the image of the Virgin of Guadalupe. Go on a weekday morning for a calmer visit, and dress respectfully; it is reachable by metro plus a short walk.

signature.name: Templo Mayor
signature.detail: The excavated Aztec main temple sits right beside the Zocalo, giving a striking sense of the city's layered past. Combine it with the cathedral next door and go early to avoid midday heat.

signature.name: Palacio de Bellas Artes
signature.detail: This marble palace is the city's cultural showpiece, with murals and a grand theater hall. Check the schedule for performances, or simply admire the exterior and the neighboring Alameda park.

signature.name: Angel of Independence
signature.detail: The golden angel on Paseo de la Reforma is the city's most recognizable monument and a lively gathering point. Visit at dusk when it is lit, and use the nearby metro or a short walk along the avenue.

food: Casual meal $8-15; street tacos a few dollars
transport: Metro about $0.30 a ride; taxis and rideshares cheap
